kfx vs azw3 which format should i use for kindle

已完成
2秒

Use AZW3 for straightforward USB sideloading; choose KFX if you want better typography and don’t mind extra conversion setup. On a compatible Kindle, KFX offers the more polished reading experience, but AZW3 is easier to work with for personal ebooks.
wikipedia
+2

What’s the difference?
	AZW3	KFX
Reading appearance	Good formatting, including rich layouts and embedded fonts	Enhanced typesetting, including automatic hyphenation, kerning, and ligatures
Converting your own books	Simpler workflow in Calibre	Calibre conversion uses the additional KFX Output plugin
Compatibility	Broader support across older Kindle models	Requires a Kindle model and firmware that support KFX
Best reason to choose it	Convenience and compatibility	Better text layout and spacing

The format and compatibility differences are documented in the Kindle format overview; the KFX conversion workflow is described by the KFX plugin developer on MobileRead.
wikipedia
+2

My recommendation

For a modern Kindle, if you’re willing to configure KFX conversion, use KFX—especially if uneven spacing in justified text bothers you. Its enhanced typesetting is the main advantage.
wikipedia
+1

If you just want to convert a book, copy it over USB, and read, use AZW3. It supports rich formatting without the additional KFX conversion workflow.
kfxtool
+1

If your books are already in AZW3 and look good, there’s little reason to convert your entire library solely for typography. KFX’s benefit is improved presentation, not a requirement for readable, well-formatted books.
wikipedia
